title: Quartic Certificates for Pure-State Tomography with Pauli Measurements
authors: Hengjian Li, Baisong Sun, Bei Zeng
abstract: Full Pauli-basis tomography of an arbitrary $n$-qubit state uses the expectation values of all nonidentity Pauli observables. For multiqubit systems, prior knowledge that the state is pure allows some of these observables to be omitted while retaining uniqueness. We study two resulting notions of uniqueness: whether every pure state is uniquely determined among pure states (UDP), and whether every pure state is uniquely determined among all states, including mixed states (UDA). We derive quartic uniqueness certificates from the fourth elementary symmetric polynomial of operators in the real span of the omitted Pauli observables. An exact quartic identity shows that, for $n$-qubit systems with $n\geq 3$, every pure state is UDA whenever the omitted Pauli observables contain no four distinct operators that commute pairwise and multiply to $\pm I$. For three qubits, this condition is also necessary for UDP, yielding an exact characterization of both UDP and UDA. We further prove that UDP and UDA coincide for any number of qubits whenever the omitted Pauli observables commute pairwise. These results provide directly checkable structural criteria for certifying pure-state tomography from restricted Pauli measurements.
summary: This paper develops structural criteria to ensure that measuring only a subset of Pauli observables on $n$ qubits is sufficient to uniquely determine the quantum state. It introduces a 'quartic certificate' based on the omitted observables and proves that avoiding certain commuting sets of four operators guarantees unique determination for $n \ge 3$. This provides a powerful, testable tool for quantum tomography protocols.
main_problem: The paper aims to derive structural criteria to guarantee that quantum state tomography, performed using restricted Pauli measurements on $n$-qubit systems, uniquely determines the quantum state (either among pure states or among all possible states).
main_result: It establishes that for $n \ge 3$, universal unique determination among all states (UDA) is guaranteed if the set of omitted Pauli observables avoids containing four distinct operators that commute pairwise and multiply to $\pm I$ (the 'four-set-free' condition).
method: The analysis converts the uniqueness problem into spectral conditions on the measurement kernel operator, deriving a 'quartic certificate' based on the fourth elementary symmetric polynomial of the operator's eigenvalues.
model_or_system: The system is an $n$-qubit quantum system, and the measurements are restricted to expectation values of a subset of Pauli observables. The ambiguity is characterized by the kernel operator $K_A$ acting on the space of state differences.
key_observables: Expectation values of Pauli observables, the measurement kernel operator $A$, and the fourth elementary symmetric polynomial $e_4(A)$.
important_parameters: The number of qubits ($n$), the structure of the omitted Pauli observables (e.g., 'four-set-free'), and the spectral properties of the kernel operator (e.g., number of positive/negative eigenvalues).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on relating the ambiguity to the spectral properties of the kernel operator $A$, and specific results are derived for $n=3$ qubits where the four-set-free condition is necessary.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by defining the uniqueness notions (UDP/UDA), deriving the quartic certificate from the spectral analysis of the kernel, establishing the structural criterion (four-set-freeness) for $n \ge 3$, and finally analyzing the necessary and sufficient conditions for $n=3$ and the general commuting case.
why_interesting: This work provides rigorous, checkable mathematical criteria directly applicable to experimental quantum information protocols, linking algebraic constraints (quartic identities) to fundamental physical properties (state distinguishability).
